reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's concern for the Hebrew people's wellbeing through multiple actions: (1) Elijah and Elisha are sent as prophets to guide Israel away from idolatry toward proper worship of Yahweh; (2) Elisha directly heals the contaminated waters at Jericho, explicitly stating 'Thus says Yahweh, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from there any more death and miscarriage' (וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר וַיֹּֽאמֶר כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה רִפִּ֙אתִי֙ לַמַּ֣יִם הָאֵ֔לֶּה), demonstrating active concern for practical wellbeing. The judgments against unfaithfulness (King Ahaziah's death, consumption of soldiers by fire) are presented as necessary corrections aimed at redirecting the people toward faithfulness, consistent with a parent's discipline of wayward children. The overall arc shows Yahweh as invested in Israel's spiritual and material welfare.
